learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the basic architecture of a computer, the difference between hardware and software, and how memory manages data!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The Central Processing Unit (CPU) is the brain of the computer. It consists of the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) for calculations, the Control Unit (CU) to manage operations, and Registers for quick data storage.
Input devices (keyboard, mouse, scanner) send data into the computer. Output devices (monitor, printer, speaker) display or produce the processed results.
Memory stores data. Primary Memory (RAM, ROM) is fast but limited; RAM is volatile (loses data when powered off). Secondary Memory (Hard Drive, SSD, USB) stores data permanently.
Hardware is the physical, tangible parts of the computer. Software is a set of instructions (programs) that tells the hardware what to do.
System Software (like Windows or Linux) runs the computer hardware. Application Software (like MS Word or a web browser) performs specific tasks for the user.

fun_activity.title: 🖥️ Build Your Dream PC
fun_activity.instructions: Make a list of components you would buy to build a gaming or programming PC. Identify which parts are Input, Output, Processing (CPU), and Storage devices!

exam_tips: 📌 Always clearly distinguish between RAM (volatile, temporary) and ROM (non-volatile, permanent).
📌 Know the three main parts of a CPU: ALU, Control Unit, and Registers.
📌 Differentiate between System Software (OS) and Application Software (Apps).
quick_recap: ⭐ The CPU processes instructions, performs calculations, and manages the flow of information.
⭐ Cache memory is a very high-speed memory placed between the CPU and RAM.
⭐ An Operating System acts as an interface between the user and the computer hardware.
